# Central Asia AI Education Audit 2026

> Open dataset: 31 leading universities across Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan,
> Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, audited for (a) public AI usage
> policy and (b) AI degree programs/courses offered.
---
> By Study Intelligence, Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS) — https://aclas.si. License: CC-BY-4.0.
> Snapshot: 2026-10-14.

## What questions does this answer?

1. Does the university publish a public, university-level AI usage policy?
2. What AI-related degree programs or courses does it verifiably offer?

## Key findings

- 6 of 31 (19%) publish a verifiable public AI policy — 4 of 6 are Kazakh.
- 18 of 31 (58%) offer a verifiable AI-named degree program or AI course
  portfolio: institutions teach AI ~3x faster than they govern it.
- Zero campus-wide AI bans.
- Turkmenistan and Tajikistan are near-complete blind spots (0 of 7).
- 81% UNVERIFIABLE rate — a finding about transparency as much as adoption.

## Files

- `central-asia-ai-policies-2026.csv` — 31 rows: AI policy per university
- `central-asia-ai-programs-2026.csv` — 31 rows: AI programs/courses
- `central-asia-ai-education-audit-2026.json` — both tables + metadata
- `METHODOLOGY.md` — sample selection, definitions, caveats
- `parse.py` — exact script that generated CSV/JSON
- `CITATION.cff` — machine-readable citation
